title: Expanding and Factorising (KS3)
subject: Maths
strapline: Two opposite skills: removing brackets and putting them back.
facts: Expanding means multiplying out brackets: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
To expand two brackets (x + 2)(x + 3), multiply every term in the first by every term in the second: x² + 5x + 6.
Factorising is the reverse of expanding — putting brackets back by taking out a common factor.
For 6x + 9, the highest common factor is 3, so it factorises to 3(2x + 3).
Always take out the highest common factor, including any common letters: 4x² + 8x = 4x(x + 2).
Check a factorisation by expanding it again — you should get back what you started with.
teacher_tips: Present expanding and factorising as inverse processes, side by side.
A grid/area model makes double-bracket expansion reliable.
Stress taking the HIGHEST common factor, not just any factor.
